name: Stiperstones
text: The Stiperstones (Welsh: Carneddau Teon) is a distinctive hill in Shropshire, England. The quartzite rock of the ridge formed some 480 million years ago. During the last Ice Age Stiperstones lay on the eastern margin of the Welsh ice sheet.

depictions.name: Stiperstones
depictions.text: The Stiperstones, alternatively Stiperstanas is a distinctive hill in Shropshire, England, noted for its various tors of quartzite that included Manstone Rock. Circa 874, the Vikings Eivor Varinsdottir and Ivarr the Boneless brought the defeated King Rhodri up to Manstone Rock on the hill. There, Ivarr executed Rhodri via the blood eagle ritual and challenged Eivor to a fight to the death, revealing himself as the murderer of Ceolbert to guilt the shieldmaiden into fighting him.
